title: Repscript program
description: A Repscript training program: a mapping with the fields repscript, id, revision, title and workouts. Example: repscript: 0, id: home-strength, revision: 1, title: Home strength, workouts: [{id: A, blocks: [{exercise: pushup, sets: 3, reps: 10}]}].

repscript.description: The format version, an integer. 0 is the draft version used until the first release. Example: repscript: 0

id.description: The program's id, a short string that identifies it. Example: id: home-strength

revision.description: The program's version number, a whole number starting at 1. Example: revision: 1

title.description: The program's title shown to the user, a string. Example: title: Home strength

notes.description: Notes on the program for the person training, a string. Example: notes: Add weight when every set reaches the top of the range.

source.description: Where the program comes from, a string. Example: source: Coach's sheet, October 2026

author.description: Who wrote the program, a string. Example: author: Alex

language.description: The language of the program's texts, a code such as en or ru. Example: language: en

goal.description: What the program trains for, one of strength, hypertrophy, power, muscular_endurance and health. It is the training adaptation, not the person's own wish such as losing weight: write the wish in notes and choose the adaptation that serves it. Example: goal: hypertrophy

schedule.description: How the workouts are spread over time, a mapping. For now it holds only per_week. Example: schedule: {per_week: 3}

per_week.description: The number of workouts in a week, a whole number or a range. The workouts follow in list order, then from the first again. Examples: per_week: 3, per_week: 3-4

exercises.description: The program's own exercises, for those the catalog does not have: a list of entries, each with an id starting with my. and names. Example: exercises: [{id: my.towel_pullup, names: {en: Towel pull-up}}]

items.description: An exercise entry: a mapping with id and names, and optionally aliases, equipment, muscles, deprecated and replaced_by. Example: {id: my.towel_pullup, names: {en: Towel pull-up}, equipment: [pullup_bar], muscles: {primary: [lats], secondary: [forearms]}}

id.description: The exercise's id: lowercase Latin letters, digits, _ and dots. An own exercise's id starts with my. Example: id: my.towel_pullup

names.description: The exercise's names by language: a mapping from a two-letter language code to the name, with at least one name. Example: names: {en: Towel pull-up, de: Handtuch-Klimmzug}

^[a-z]{2}$.description: The exercise's name in this language, a string. Example: en: Towel pull-up

aliases.description: Other names of the exercise, a list of strings in any language. Example: aliases: [towel pull-ups]

items.description: Another name of the exercise, a string. Example: towel pull-ups

equipment.description: What the exercise needs: a list of keys from catalog/equipment.yaml, or [] when it needs nothing. Example: equipment: [pullup_bar]

items.description: An equipment key from catalog/equipment.yaml, a string. Example: pullup_bar

muscles.description: The muscles the exercise works: primary for those that do the work, secondary for those that help, each a list of keys from catalog/muscles.yaml. Example: muscles: {primary: [lats], secondary: [biceps]}

primary.description: The muscles that do the work: a list of at least one key from catalog/muscles.yaml. Example: primary: [lats]

items.description: A muscle key from catalog/muscles.yaml, a string. Example: lats

secondary.description: The muscles that help: a list of keys from catalog/muscles.yaml. Example: secondary: [biceps]

items.description: A muscle key from catalog/muscles.yaml, a string. Example: lats

deprecated.description: deprecated: true marks an exercise that another one replaces, named in replaced_by. Example: deprecated: true

replaced_by.description: The id of the exercise that replaces this one, together with deprecated: true. Example: replaced_by: pullup.wide

workouts.description: The program's workouts, a list of at least one mapping, each with an id and blocks. Example: workouts: [{id: A, blocks: [{exercise: pushup, sets: 3, reps: 10}]}]

items.description: A workout, a mapping with an id and a list of blocks. Example: {id: A, blocks: [{exercise: pushup, sets: 3, reps: 10}]}

id.description: The workout's id, a short string that names it within the program. Example: id: A

title.description: The workout's title shown to the user, a string. Example: title: Heavy upper body

notes.description: Notes on the workout, a string. Example: notes: Warm up the shoulders first.

blocks.description: The workout's exercises in order, a list of at least one block. Example: blocks: [{exercise: pushup, sets: 3, reps: 10}]

items.description: A block, all sets of one exercise: a mapping with exercise, sets, and reps or time. Example: {exercise: pushup, sets: 3, reps: 8-12, rest: 90s}

exercise.description: The exercise's id: a catalog id from catalog/index.yaml, or the id of an own exercise described in exercises, starting with my. Example: exercise: pullup.wide

sets.description: The number of sets, a whole number or a range. Examples: sets: 3, sets: 3-4

reps.description: The repetitions in each set: a whole number, a range, a minimum followed by + (then as many as possible), or max (as many as possible). Examples: reps: 10, reps: 8-12, reps: 5+, reps: max

time.description: The duration of each set, for timed exercises such as a plank: a whole number with the unit s, m or h, minutes:seconds, or a range. Examples: time: 30s, time: 1:30, time: 30-45s

rest.description: The rest after each set: a whole number with the unit s, m or h, minutes:seconds, or a range. Examples: rest: 90s, rest: 1:30, rest: 2-3m

load.description: The weight of each set: kg or lb for an external weight, or bw: true for body weight, with add_kg or add_lb for extra weight, and optionally implement for what carries it. Examples: load: {kg: 18}, load: {bw: true, add_kg: 5}

kg.description: An external weight in kilograms: a number with a dot for decimals, or a range. Examples: kg: 18, kg: 2.5, kg: 16-20

lb.description: An external weight in pounds: a number with a dot for decimals, or a range. Examples: lb: 40, lb: 35-45

bw.description: Body weight: bw: true means the exercise is done with body weight. Example: bw: true

add_kg.description: Extra weight in kilograms on top of body weight (a vest, a belt): a number or a range, together with bw: true. Example: add_kg: 2-5

add_lb.description: Extra weight in pounds on top of body weight (a vest, a belt): a number or a range, together with bw: true. Example: add_lb: 10

implement.description: What carries the weight: a key from catalog/equipment.yaml, such as dumbbells or backpack. The weight is that of one implement. Example: implement: dumbbells
